København is a Danish municipality featured in the clinical quality reports for atrial fibrillation treatment in Denmark. It is included in the detailed municipal breakdowns of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) annual reports, which serve as essential tools for local quality development and benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system.

In the 2022–2023 annual report, København's data regarding stroke events among atrial fibrillation patients is utilized in the DanStroke-based calculations for Indicator 5, which measures the prevention of ischemic stroke via anticoagulation treatment [^src1]. The municipality is also geographically and administratively categorized within the broader healthcare framework, specifically as a municipality comprised by the [[sundhedsklynge|Sundhedsklynge]] (health cluster) "Byen København" [^src2]. 

The inclusion of København in these reports highlights its role in the national monitoring of clinical quality, where data from both the National Patient Registry (LPR) and the Danish Stroke Registry (DanStroke) are analyzed at the municipal level to assess treatment outcomes and adherence to clinical guidelines.
